summary: Clarifies BGP origin validation based on RPKI. Deployment has been hampered by vendor misimplementations about which routes are validated and whether policy is applied when not configured, and this document explains the intended behavior.

plainLanguage.summary: Routers were checking route ownership in different ways. This spells out the rules so everyone checks in the same way.

questions: how does bgp origin validation work
what does rpki validation state mean
how should routers handle invalid routes
subtitle: Clarify the rules for checking BGP route origin with RPKI

tldr.problem: BGP vendors implemented RPKI origin validation differently: some only validated certain routes, and some applied policy without operator configuration. These misimplementations made deployment chaotic and vulnerable to misconfiguration.
tldr.mechanism: The clarification states that routers MUST evaluate and set the validation state for ALL routes from any source (eBGP, iBGP, redistribution) unless configured otherwise, and policy MUST NOT be applied without explicit operator configuration.
tldr.outcome: Consistent implementation across vendors ensures operators can drop invalid routes from any source and maintain full control over routing policy decisions.

today: RFC 8481 clarifies RFC 6811 to ensure consistent vendor implementation of RPKI origin validation. It was updated by RFC 9324.

sections.title: The Implementation Problem
sections.content:
RPKI-based BGP origin validation (RFC 6811) assigns each route a validation state: NotFound, Valid, or Invalid. Deployment has been hampered by vendor misimplementations in two critical areas: which routes are validated and whether policy is applied when not specified by configuration.

These differences mean operators cannot reliably drop invalid routes coming from every potential source, making the network vulnerable to misconfiguration and route hijacking.
sections.plainLanguage: Vendors built the feature differently, so operators could not rely on it working the same way everywhere.

sections.title: Evaluate All Routes
sections.content:
A router MUST evaluate and set the validation state of all routes in BGP coming from any source (eBGP, iBGP, or redistribution from static or connected routes), unless specifically configured otherwise by the operator. When redistributing from other sources, the router uses the router's own BGP AS number (or a configured value for confederation or multi-AS setups).

Implementations MAY provide configuration options to control which routes are validated, but validation is the default behavior.
sections.plainLanguage: Check every route, no matter where it comes from. Only skip checking if the operator says to skip.

sections.title: Operator Control of Policy
sections.content: Once routes are evaluated and have their state set, the operator is in complete control of any policy applied based on that state. Policy MUST NOT be applied without explicit operator configuration. Automatic policy actions (such as those in RFC 8097) MUST NOT happen unless the operator specifically configures them.
sections.plainLanguage: The router sets the validation state and tells the operator. The operator decides what to do about it.

sections.title: Impact
sections.content: These clarifications are critical for secure routing. RPKI deployment depends on consistent, predictable behavior. With this standard, operators can trust that their RPKI configuration works the same way across different vendor implementations and network sources.
sections.plainLanguage: When everyone checks the same way, the system is more secure and operators know what to expect.
